artifacts.name: agent-guidelines
artifacts.description: Authoritative project guide for agents and contributors, curated to a 6,000-token budget: it carries the rules needed on nearly every task and routes to the reference docs for everything else (see its Detail Docs index). Inline: the worker-first shape (the bus consumer is the primary process; FastAPI /health is dev-only), the co-core wheelhouse mechanism (gs://co-gcs-pypi via [tool.uv] find-links, not PyPI) and the load-bearing patch floor, the SocratiCode code-exploration policy (trimmed to the negative rule and a three-row table, with the full reference in docs/SOCRATICODE.md), the hard boundary between /etc/replicator/.env and the repo .env, the Redis >=7.0 floor and co-broker (CannObserv/broker), which Replicator is only ever a client of, the bus rules that bind every change (at-least-once idempotency with two keys, store-then-publish, read(count=1), fail-loud from_wire with a global dispatch table, DLQ vs retry, no outbox on the consume path, the three stream kinds, Watcher as content.fetch's only issuer with seed_fetch.py confined to scratch streams, the normative contracts), the common commands, and the commit/logging/date conventions. Everything else is routed from its Detail Docs index, which names each reference doc and what a task would need it for; that index is the roster, not this description.

artifacts.name: readme
artifacts.description: Top-level README. What Replicator is within the Cannabis Observer cluster: the command -> fetch -> fingerprint -> temp-store -> fact loop, content.fetch-policy as the third stream kind, why the worker rather than the API is the deployed process, setup via the wheelhouse sync, the two-env-file boundary with a table of only what this VM overrides (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md is the authoritative variable reference), the deployed loop proven by Watcher's traffic in the journal rather than by a seeded command (the --production example retired in #90), seed_fetch.py on scratch streams, the dev server and why it needs --log-config, and the systemd deploy recipe.

artifacts.name: design-plans
artifacts.description: Founding MVP design (2026-06-25, adopted). The command/fact contracts as shipped in co-core v0.7.0 — ContentFetchCommand (URL-addressed, command_id as the wire idempotency key) and BlobAvailableEvent (content_fingerprint, blob_uri, size_bytes, media_type, url, optional command_id) — the stream taxonomy and DLQ naming, the temp-storage interface, the two-level idempotency argument, why fingerprint parity dissolves when Replicator is the sole fetcher, explicit MVP scope cuts, and the build sequence. The founding plan's three open questions were settled 2026-07-31 in a companion doc: blob_uri is a file:// URI over a two-level sharded, content-addressed path (<blob_dir>/<ab>/<cd>/<sha256>.bin, constant .bin extension, temp-file + os.replace so presence means complete); the MVP command issuer is an in-repo scripts/seed_fetch.py rather than Watcher or Archiver; and the MVP boundary is stop-at-fact, with archiver-writeback reclassified from MVP+ to won't-do — Archiver consumes blob_available and writes the SourceRevision itself (archiver#118, which also carries the info_source_id contract gap). Blob retention is out of MVP scope and tracked in #5. Also holds the relocated resolution of the fetch_failed open question (2026-07-31, moved out of the issuer contract in #24): the consumer arrived in watcher#241, co-core shipped FetchFailedEvent in v0.7.2, and the resolution deliberately did NOT ship non-terminal facts (#9 §3, unbounded growth on an untrimmed broadcast stream) and deliberately left the rows with no usable command_id DLQ-only, because a fact naming no command closes nothing and one naming a foreign command_id would be worse than silence.

artifacts.name: issuer-contract
artifacts.description: Normative contract for any service publishing content.fetch commands (Watcher since watcher#241; seed_fetch.py on scratch streams) — and its permanent home, linked to rather than copied by issuer-side repos. The read-through third of a three-file contract: issuer-reference carries the request side and outcome-reference the result side, all three normative, and the path sibling repos link is this one. Opens with the frame rule (rule zero): publish through to_wire and never hand-roll the fields — an XADD of top-level command_id/url fails from_wire into content.fetch.dlq silently; both facts are keyed per occurrence and correlation rides on the payload's command_id, never the envelope key (the six keys and the key rules are in issuer-reference). Then the payload: the ContentFetchCommand table with the tz-aware occurred_at rule, the request-options summary (refused not adjusted, identity untouched) pointing at the refusal list, and The facts — blob_available and fetch_failed on content.blobs, tabulated in outcome-reference, with the three rules every consumer needs (branch on terminal first, not_modified is a success, None means nobody said). Then the eight MUSTs, which are the contract proper: mint a fresh ULID command_id per fetch occasion (a resource-stable id is silently deduped away for 24h); persist the command_id -> domain map before publishing; url is not a correlation key; correlation must be idempotent because one command can yield more than one fact; never dedupe an inbox on content_fingerprint; handle fetch_failed but keep a reaper, because five conditions still produce nothing; copy the bytes within the at-least-seven-day window, which runs from last fetch reference, and branch on blob_uri's scheme; and send no validator until the consumer handles not_modified. Closes with what Replicator guarantees (store-then-publish, announce-then-ack, command_id and info_source_id echoed, the fingerprint is definitional, at-least-once) and what it does not. Written for #8, split for #24, rebalanced across its references in #111.

artifacts.name: issuer-reference
artifacts.description: Request half of the content.fetch issuer reference, split out of the contract in #24 and split again from the outcome half (outcome-reference) when one file outgrew a single read. Equally normative — a rule does not become advisory by living here. Carries mostly what an issuer looks up BEFORE publishing a command — and, for balance with the outcome half, the turnaround pacing adds and what losing the command_id map costs. The request-options rules (#11): header names are lower-cased before the merge so the issuer wins rather than httpx sending two User-Agent lines, surrounding whitespace is dropped from a value and nothing else, and the full refusal list, where every entry is refused rather than adjusted with a terminal fetch_failed / invalid_request_options before any request goes out (hop-by-hop headers, host and content-length which httpx derives, any proxy-*, names that are not RFC 9110 tokens, values with any byte outside \x20-\x7e because a CRLF is request splitting, two names differing only in case, more than 32 headers or 8192 bytes of them, and timeout_seconds that is non-finite or over REPLICATOR_MAX_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS because the consume path is serial). The invalid_request_options wedge in full: it is the one refusal an issuer can wedge itself on, being terminal AND decided entirely from the command, so a stored validator that would be refused must be screened at mint time and cleared automatically on that reason alone (Watcher runs both halves: sendable_validator() and clear_validators()); #60 screens etag and last_modified before publishing them, but the header count and byte total remain the issuer's. The provenance and trust posture: content.fetch is an unauthenticated capability resting entirely on the broker's per-service ACL grants (wider than declared until CannObserv/broker#14 — replicator can XADD it too) and the Tailscale ACL; #89 declined message signing and a URL allowlist and shipped a destination guard (#95) instead, which bounds where a fetch may POINT rather than who may issue one; DNS rebinding's TOCTOU window is the stated residual; headers widen the capability and the refusal table is the cheap bound on that widening; two properties an issuer can rely on are that a refused command is refused before any request goes out and that header values never reach the journal. Also the envelope key by key — the six keys to_wire produces, the per-payload key derivation (command_id; content_fingerprint:command_id; command_id:occurred_at) and why the facts were re-keyed per occurrence (cannobserv#270, #300) — pacing at the deployed defaults (every wait is slept through unless an operator sets the interval above REPLICATOR_READ_BLOCK_MS), what losing the command_id -> domain map costs (MUST-2), the co-core version history (Replicator requires ≥ 0.8.0), and what the envelope key is operationally for.

artifacts.name: outcome-reference
artifacts.description: Outcome half of the content.fetch issuer reference — everything an issuer looks up AFTER a command is published, split from the request half (issuer-reference) when one file outgrew a single read. Equally normative. Both facts field by field — the BlobAvailableEvent table and the FetchFailedEvent table, with the reason tokens emitted today (http_status, not_modified, not_fetchable, too_large, destination_refused, unsupported_schema_version, invalid_request_options, handler_error). The reasoning behind the enriched blob_available fields: None means nobody said rather than the default (final_url is None when the driver reported no landing URL, content_type_raw when the origin sent no Content-Type — deliberately not application/octet-stream), status_code is always 2xx on this fact so a branch on == 200 silently drops a 203, verbatim excludes surrounding whitespace while an over-long or unsendable value is dropped rather than repaired (#60), and these are per-occasion values on a fact that has been keyed per occasion since cannobserv#300, which dissolves the 0.7.x stale-validator caveat. The conditional-GET trap: a matching validator earns fetch_failed / not_modified / terminal=True / status_code=304 with no blob and no DLQ entry, so a consumer without an explicit branch converts every successful no-change check into a spurious content loss — alert on fetch_failed where reason != not_modified. The full failure taxonomy table (every condition, Replicator's action, what the issuer sees) with the three classes of silent row analysed: no usable command_id (permanently silent, what MUST-6's reaper is for), silent only while in flight (#9 §3), and the duplicate-command_id row that is silent because the command already succeeded. Reading the failure fact: wrong_payload_type is in co-core's docstring but Replicator never emits it, reason is a plain str and not a Literal so the token list is additive, and everything emitted today is terminal=True. The five silent conditions in full, including a command trimmed while pending (#109). How to read the DLQ with a plain XREAD and no consumer group, why it is the complement of every FAILED close rather than every terminal one since #17, and the synthesized-record anomaly that carries no key. Why a duplicate failure fact is not identical (the fact is published before the dead-letter, so a crash in that window yields a second fetch_failed with a fresh occurred_at and therefore a different envelope key). How the blob TTL clock runs — why seven days is a stated commitment rather than a host setting (a bucket lifecycle rule on daysSinceCustomTime: 8 against a 7-day promise), from last reference by a fetch, not last read by a consumer, implemented as utime on local and customTime on gcs, with the object store's one-day lifecycle granularity being why the commitment is phrased as AT LEAST seven days and why blob_expires_at errs early. And two consequences an issuer inherits from the MUSTs: what fingerprint-dedupe now loses beyond a correlation, and re-hashing the bytes.

artifacts.name: replicate-issuer-contract
artifacts.description: Trust model and issuer obligations for content.replicate (#34), shipped for gcs by #29: the loop resolves the alias, guards both paths, writes through AsyncGcsDriver.create_if_absent and emits both facts on content.artifacts; gdrive and ia are refused provider_disabled until they have a conditional create. A status table tracks each gear-marked obligation (T1-T6, the charter invariant) from settled-ahead-of-code to shipped. States only the deltas from the content.fetch contract and its two references, which stay normative here. Why this is not the fetch capability widened, in summary — the conclusion (bus access control is proportionate) is reached again, but the escalation trigger is not; the evidence is in replicate-issuer-reference. T1: credentials_alias is a selector, never a secret — gcs via ADC, gdrive via a service account with Shared Drive membership or domain-wide delegation, ia via an archive.org keypair — so no credential field on the wire (cannobserv#303 open question 1). T2: the alias namespace is a capability namespace, bounded by an operator-provisioned allow-list in host config; the granted writer set is wider than declared until CannObserv/broker#14. T3: the issuer renders path_template and the rendered destination travels, while the host binds the container per provider; traversal and non-normalized paths are refused. T3a: never resolve blob_uri as a path — extract and validate the fingerprint and rebuild through the store, else invalid_source. T4: a redelivery never destroys an artifact — absent write, matching no-op re-emitting the same public_url, differing terminal destination_conflict — with per-provider create-if-absent primitives, and the rule applies to ia, whose PUT overwrites by default. T5: ia is public and unretractable, gated by provisioning. T6: public_url is never echoed from the command, is present only where the object is known to exist, and always names a location inside an operator-provisioned container (narrowed in #36). Its own escalation triggers, two of three met (#89) with neither answer on the wire. The MUST verdict table over the fetch obligations (1/2/4/6 verbatim, 3 adapts, 5 and 8 no analogue, 7 inverts into scheduling against blob_expires_at) plus R1-R3 (render, do not delegate; a deterministic destination per occasion; public_url not stable across occasions). What Replicator refuses: alias_unknown, provider_disabled (also a provider 403/404), invalid_destination (also a provider 400), destination_conflict, blob_expired and invalid_source; 5xx, 429, 408 and statusless failures leave the command open and publish nothing. Charter check: info_item_rep_spec_id is a second echo exemption on info_source_id's terms, and the alias is a key, never a value. Fan-out and the expired-blob policy are deliberately left open.

artifacts.name: replicate-issuer-reference
artifacts.description: Companion to the content.replicate issuer contract, equally normative, carrying the reasoning several of its clauses rest on (split out in #111). Why replication is not the fetch capability widened: the read/write comparison (direction, credentials, blast radius, self-healing, reversibility), the IAS3 evidence that an archive.org item cannot be deleted, and the #89 note that the one-localhost-broker premise is gone while the conclusion survives. Why T3a exists: blob_uri is issuer-supplied, so resolving it as a path would be a read-side traversal onto a public, undeletable destination — file:///etc/replicator/co-pypi-reader.json would publish the host's GCS reader key; locate_blob is the one consumer. T4's correction that ia means the archive.org item upload, whose PUT overwrites by default, not the append-only Wayback Machine, and why Wayback semantics would be a fourth provider. T6's first wording and why it was narrowed (#36): Blob.public_url is a client-side f-string that never round-trips. And why the Charter check predicted no exemption would be needed before co-core 0.9.4 made info_item_rep_spec_id required.

artifacts.name: boundaries-charter
artifacts.description: Normative charter for what Replicator is allowed to become — sibling to the issuer contract, which settles the wire while this settles the service. The rule: Replicator owns the mechanics of acquiring bytes from a network and holding them briefly, never why, when, or what they mean. Three tests for any proposed capability, field, or setting (durable per-resource history -> issuer; cross-command coordination over a resource only the fetcher can see -> Replicator; expressible without domain vocabulary or it is the issuer's), resolved when both fire by mechanism-to-Replicator / policy-to-the-issuer / config-over-the-bus. Worked examples: per-host politeness (the hard case, where the tests do not resolve to one side) and conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified are durable per-resource history, so the fact returns them and the next command replays them as headers — conditional GET with zero per-URL state here). Config taxonomy of three channels (env for host facts, command for the occasion, a policy stream for cluster policy needing cross-command state) with a fourth — an inbound admin HTTP API — rejected by name; ingress is read-only liveness and self-description, and the invariant that matters is asserted about the worker, which binds no port, not the dev-only FastAPI app. The policy stream SHIPPED in #19 on co-core v0.7.7 (cannobserv#285) and is named **content.fetch-policy with a hyphen** — the dotted content.fetch.policy this document originally proposed collides with the <topic>.dlq derivation of the command stream. Last-write-wins per host, replayed from 0-0 at boot via the groupless AsyncBusTailReader and tailed thereafter, MAXLEN-trimmed by the producer because periodic full republication onto an untrimmed stream is unbounded growth, a Redis hash rejected for having no schema_version and coupling to a key name. Four properties that must hold (the producer republishes the full set and MAXLEN-trims it; an unknown host resolves to a conservative default; enforcement has a rate floor the consumer must answer); the consumer-side rules that fail silently if missed, and the sleep-or-park enforcement mechanism, live in docs/POLITENESS.md. REPLICATOR_MIN_HOST_INTERVAL_SECONDS is now the FALLBACK rather than the rule, and 0 no longer disables pacing outright. Two known limitations recorded rather than omitted: blob_uri's host-local file:// coupling (#7), and the host asked for not being the host reached under redirects, which #19 did NOT resolve. Enforced by tests/test_boundaries.py in CI: eight invariants including an AST scan of src/ for domain nouns in identifiers and string literals, a recursive route walk, no locally-defined wire models (payload shapes, not producer-owned token vocabularies like FailureReason), and REPLICATOR_-prefixed settings with BUILD_ID exempted by name. Written for #12, updated for #19.

artifacts.name: architecture
artifacts.description: Founding-design pointers and the module-by-module layout of src/ (worker, storage, api, core) with the job each file owns, plus the directory map of scripts/, tests/, deploy/ and the wheelhouse. What each individual stream carries is in docs/STREAMS.md; the rules common to every stream are in docs/CONVENTIONS.md.

artifacts.name: streams
artifacts.description: The reasoning behind what each individual stream carries: the issuer contract and boundaries charter pointers, content.blobs carrying both blob_available and fetch_failed, the seven optional passthrough fields on blob_available and why None means nobody said it, one run_loop over N command streams parameterized by CommandSpec, the content.replicate loop and its create-if-absent write for gcs, alias-keyed writers and the allow-list guard order, the FailureReporter seam, per-command headers/timeout_seconds validation and why unsendable options are refused rather than clamped, a pointer to docs/POLITENESS.md for the pacer and the groupless content.fetch-policy reader, the per-occurrence fact keys, and info_source_id as an echoed field. Read this before changing what any stream carries. Split out of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; the rules common to every stream are in docs/CONVENTIONS.md.

artifacts.name: politeness
artifacts.description: Per-host politeness, the consumer-side mechanism; the boundary decision (Replicator enforces, the issuer decides, the numbers travel over the bus) and the producer's obligations are the charter's. Spending a wait: src/worker/pacing.py's host -> last-request map and handler.py::_pace — a wait up to REPLICATOR_READ_BLOCK_MS is slept through, a longer one raises TransientFetchError and parks for claim_stale, because park-only misses a 1 s interval by 60x and sleep-only blocks every other host; only a request that goes out calls record(); keyed on the host asked for, not the host reached. The content.fetch-policy stream (src/worker/policy.py): read groupless, replayed from 0-0 at boot in REPLAY_COUNT batches that degrade to count=1 around a poison frame, tailed at count=1; AsyncBusTailReader.replay() is unusable; the replay runs before the consume loop and worker ready is logged after it; four ways to apply a policy wrongly (branch on revoked first, 0.0 is legal and falsy, the default's strictness is reported per host at apply time, guard on occurred_at per host), the global from_wire table, bounded poison recovery. Escalation on 429 and 503 (#25): HostPacer.report_rate_limited raises the interval by BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER up to BACKOFF_MAX_HEADROOM above the published floor, drops it after BACKOFF_DECAY_SECONDS measured from the last refusal, honours Retry-After only upward, and publishes no fact, adds no setting and keeps no second map.

artifacts.name: bus-conventions
artifacts.description: The co-core / Redis Streams rules that hold for every stream Replicator touches, split out of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in #35: consumers are idempotent and producers own the outbox (no Postgres outbox on the consume path), the extra="ignore" validation posture and branching on schema_version before destructuring, the batch-poison caveat that forces read(count=1), dead_letter as a shipped seam and the deterministic-vs-transient split, recovering a frame that failed to decode and has no fields, from_wire's global dispatch table, claim_stale as the retry path and why it takes count=1, XPENDING times_delivered as the retry counter, why an absent XINFO CONSUMERS entry is not evidence a worker is down, the failing-message vs failing-cycle distinction and the backoff ceiling, injection-only bus clients, store-then-publish, tz-aware UTC occurred_at, from_wire's keyword-only topic/message_id, and where sha256 lives in co_core. Also the rule an agent needs before touching the content.replicate write path for gcs (#29), and the replicator:cmd:* keys (#80). What a particular stream carries is in docs/STREAMS.md; adaptive per-host politeness (#25) is in docs/POLITENESS.md.

artifacts.name: temp-storage
artifacts.description: The blob tree: file://<blob_dir>/<ab>/<cd>/<sha256>.bin with a constant .bin extension, temp-file + os.replace so presence means complete, and creation-only 0644/0755 modes with the startup reachability warning. Retention: the TTL runs from last reference (os.utime on the store short-circuit), the three populations under REPLICATOR_BLOB_DIR and why in-flight .tmp files are not garbage, the byte ceiling as backpressure rather than a faster clock, the single BlobUsage with two writers, orphan recording, and why the sweep runs in the worker rather than a systemd timer. Carries the REPLICATOR_BLOB_* variables and REPLICATOR_MAX_BLOB_BYTES themselves since #92, under ## Variables; docs/ENVIRONMENT.md indexes them by name.

artifacts.name: infrastructure-topology
artifacts.description: Where this service runs and what it talks to, as opposed to how its unit starts (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md): the dedicated co-replicator VM and its ports, the broker being co-broker with Replicator a client that never ships one and the Redis >=7.0 floor that follows, the shared SocratiCode store on co-index with its full-MagicDNS Qdrant URL, unauthenticated Ollama, the collection names projectId fixes and the one-host-per-projectId rule (#92), and the temp-blob and test buckets on either side of the test/production line with the grants that distinguish them.

artifacts.name: deployment-reference
artifacts.description: VM topology and ports, the systemd unit's lifecycle and its ExecStartPre guards, the checkout guard, and the co-core pin. The environment variables themselves are in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md. Also OOMScoreAdjust=-900 on both units (#92): on exe.dev everything descended from a session inherits oom_score_adj=-1000 and is exempt from the OOM killer, so an unprotected worker at ~670 was what the kernel would pick under pressure the dev tooling created. tailscaled gets the same -900 by drop-in (#113), and MemoryLow= on the worker and tailscaled is real only through the system.slice.d grant, since cgroup2 here has no memory_recursiveprot.

artifacts.name: failure-notification-reference
artifacts.description: What replicator.service reports when it fails, split out of docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (#99). The OnFailure=replicator-failure-notify@%n.service handler: the CRITICAL journal record it always writes, and the POST it makes only when REPLICATOR_NOTIFY_URL is set — unset is the shipped posture and a working one. The six REPLICATOR_NOTIFY_* variables, read by the handler and never by the worker, which is why they are not in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md. Notifier mode vs webhook mode, the idempotency key built from MONITOR_INVOCATION_ID and why a key is never reused, and delivery scored on the 202 body's status rather than the 202 itself. Read the journal with `journalctl -t replicator-failure`, never `-u`, because %n doubles the unit suffix.

artifacts.name: environment-variables
artifacts.description: Every environment variable Replicator reads, indexed in one place, with the reasoning behind each default — except the blob and temp-store settings, whose reasoning sits beside the behaviour it argues about in docs/STORAGE.md (#92). Also the hard boundary between /etc/replicator/.env (the only file the service reads) and the repo .env (dev/agent secrets). Split out of docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. Since #92 a third carrier is documented alongside them: .claude/settings.json holds the six non-secret values addressing the shared SocratiCode store and .claude/settings.local.json holds QDRANT_API_KEY, both read by the agent harness and by nothing the service starts.

artifacts.name: testing-reference
artifacts.description: Test layout — the mirror rule, splitting by concern rather than by helper, and the _integration filename exception — plus how the bus is tested: the fake_redis fixture and what it is sound for, the two places fakeredis diverges from the live broker (it registers a consumer on an empty XREADGROUP; it ignores block), the real_redis fixture with its db-0 refusal and auth-failure re-raise, the scratch_topic confinement, and the one namespace outside replicator.itest.* that an end-to-end run creates.

artifacts.name: style-logging
artifacts.description: The logging stack: build_json_formatter() as the single schema definition installed two ways (configure_logging on the root logger, and src/core/log_config.json naming the same factory for uvicorn), why the worker needs no --log-config, the two plain-text journald lines the wheelhouse-sync ExecStartPre writes and why they cannot be JSON, and why the color_message strip is a filter on the loggers rather than on the formatter or the handler.

artifacts.name: commands
artifacts.description: Canonical command reference: the wheelhouse sync that must precede uv sync, env loading, running the worker locally with a distinct consumer name, the dev /health server on port 8001, test and lint invocations, Redis bus inspection (XINFO STREAM/GROUPS/CONSUMERS and DLQ length), submodule and doctor repair, and the systemd install/restart recipe. Since #92 it also carries the SocratiCode block: the offline validate-store / validate-manifest gates, preflight run bare, every server launch wrapped in a systemd-run memory cap, and the operator-machine recipe for installing the Qdrant API key on stdin.

artifacts.name: skills-doc
artifacts.description: Agent skills index. The two-level symlink chain (.claude/skills -> skills/ -> skills-vendor/) and why it lets a local override shadow a vendor skill in both discovery systems, the vendor submodules, the local brainstorming override and its required override frontmatter, the once-per-day SessionStart submodule refresh hook, which pushes the commit it makes (skills#293), and its suspension for the v1.2 curating-context hold, the write-guard hook that dangles on a submodule-less checkout, and how CI handles submodules — the test job checks out skills-vendor/ because test_skills_hook.py dereferences the hook symlink while lint does not need it, with the cost, the pinned-SHA semantics against the v1.2 hold, and the checkout-time failure mode accepted in exchange (#27). Also the two files that tailor shipping-work's Step 1.5 doc-check gate — .skills/doc-sensitive-paths (what it watches, #75) and .skills/doc-sections (the docs it names on a hit, #93) — and the pytest guard behind each.

artifacts.name: socraticode-reference
artifacts.description: The on-demand half of the Code Exploration Policy, now describing a store this VM does not host: Qdrant and Ollama run on co-index and Docker is disabled here (#92). Split out of AGENTS.md in #35 to match gregoryfoster/skills#115: the full ten-row tool-selection table, the deferred-tool prefetch and the SessionStart hook that prints it, per-tool gotchas (codebase_search ranks by embedding similarity so an empty result is a threshold miss not an absence; the graph answers empty rather than erroring when stale; codebase_context_search only sees files listed in the manifest; the file watcher is ephemeral), cross-repo search over the four cohort siblings via linkedProjects in .socraticode.json (relative entries, the one source since skills#287) and the three ways a linked repo contributes nothing without saying so, graph-yield health, and .socraticodeignore index scope. Owned by init-socraticode and overwritten wholesale on a re-run; repo-specific exploration notes live in AGENTS.md under Code Exploration Notes (repo-specific).

artifacts.name: deployment-topology
artifacts.description: systemd unit running the worker (not the API). Ordering After=tailscaled.service only, never Wants=/Requires= (#88; the broker is reached by tailnet name), the BUILD_ID stamp written by ExecStartPre, the deliberate absence of the repo .env from the EnvironmentFile chain (it holds GitHub PATs the worker never needs), the hard Redis >=7.0 floor guard, the main-checkout guard that refuses to start the service off any branch but main, or off a main carrying unpushed commits (#37, #48, scripts/check_main_checkout.sh, overridable with REPLICATOR_ALLOW_ANY_CHECKOUT=1) and sits ahead of the BUILD_ID stamp, the non-fatal wheelhouse sync, StateDirectory, and bounded restarts. OOMScoreAdjust=-900 (#92) makes the worker the last thing this VM's OOM killer chooses rather than the first — not -1000, which is exemption and would make a leaking worker unreclaimable. MemoryLow=128M (#113) is a reservation, never a cap, and inert without deploy/system.slice.d/replicator-memory.conf.

artifacts.name: wheelhouse-sync
artifacts.description: Mirrors the private cannobserv package index (gs://co-gcs-pypi/wheels/) into ./.wheelhouse, from which uv resolves co-core and co-core-aio via find-links. Must run before uv sync and must not import the project, since the project's deps are what it provides — hence the isolated `uv run --no-project --with google-cloud-storage` invocation. ADC auth: the SA key on the VM, keyless WIF in CI.

artifacts.name: redis-floor-guard
artifacts.description: ExecStartPre guard asserting the Redis >=7.0 change-bus server floor. Replicator is the cluster's first user of AsyncBusConsumer.claim_stale, which reads XAUTOCLAIM's three-element reply — the deleted-ids element added in Redis server 7.0 — so a lower version breaks crash recovery. Soft on an unreachable broker (it may still be starting), fatal on a genuine downgrade.

artifacts.name: ci-pipeline
artifacts.description: GitHub Actions CI. Concurrency keyed on github.sha rather than github.ref (#44), so a push that lands several commits gets a run per commit instead of cancelling all but the last and leaving the intermediate ones unattested. Keyless Workload Identity Federation auth to GCP for the wheelhouse mirror, a fail-fast guard asserting the GCP_WIF_PROVIDER org variable is visible to this repo, ruff check and format gates, a co-core extras import smoke proving [extract] and [bus] wire up in a clean environment, and pytest with the coverage gate. Deliberately no Postgres service and no alembic steps — Replicator is DB-free. The test job's checkout carries `submodules: true` and the lint job deliberately does not (#27): tests/test_skills_hook.py dereferences the .claude/hooks/ symlink into skills-vendor/, and actions/checkout fetches no submodules by default, so without the key that test cannot pass in CI at all — it failed identically on every commit and main was red from 7bf5988 until the fix. Ruff extend-excludes skills-vendor/, so lint never reads what it never fetches. Costs ~2.2s of a ~1m10s job; checkout resolves the SHA pinned in this superproject rather than upstream tip, so it is independent of the v1.2 skills hold. Reasoning in docs/SKILLS.md.

artifacts.name: dependency-contract
artifacts.description: Project and tooling contract. The co-core / co-core-aio pins (>=0.10,<0.11) with their [extract] and [bus] extras, the [tool.uv] find-links wheelhouse resolution, the ruff rule set and its skills-vendor exclusion, the ty exclusion, the replicator-worker console script, pytest configuration (asyncio auto mode, integration marker, timeout) and the 80% coverage gate.

artifacts.name: main-checkout-guard
artifacts.description: ExecStartPre guard refusing to start replicator.service from any checkout but main (#37). The main checkout IS the deployment on this host, so a worktree switch or a left-behind branch silently deploys unmerged code. Refuses on a non-main branch, a detached or unborn HEAD, a directory that is not a work tree, and git's dubious-ownership refusal (which gets its own message and remedy, since it means the directory is a repository but not this user's). Also refuses when main is ahead of origin/main (#48): unpushed commits are on no shared branch, and unlike the behind case that verdict does not need the cached ref to be fresh, because origin/main is moved by a successful push from this repository as well as by fetch. Warns without refusing when the checkout is behind origin/main, when there is no origin/main ref to compare against, or when the tree is dirty. REPLICATOR_ALLOW_ANY_CHECKOUT=1, the literal 1 only, overrides. Behaviour is pinned by tests/test_check_main_checkout.py against throwaway git repos.
